title: Cross-attention versus joint attention
hook: How the picture reads the prompt in a U-Net and in a transformer. In one the text never changes. In the other the text is updated too, and image tokens see each other in the same step.

verified.claim: CrossAttention takes q from x and k and v from context, and returns only x's update.
BasicTransformerBlock runs attn1 then attn2, and attn1 uses context None, so it is self-attention.
_block_mixing and DoubleStreamBlock concatenate text and image q, k, v, attend once, then split.
Each stream has its own q, k, v projections.
Flux joins the streams for its single blocks, and in MMDiT a pre_only last context block drops the text after that step.
The shapes, the unchanged text and the pair counts.
The paper's abstract describes separate weights and a bidirectional flow between image and text tokens.

unchecked: The draft said joint attention is necessary for text in pictures and cross-attention is weaker. We removed both. The paper reports better text and typography for its whole model, which isn't a test of attention alone.
The pair counts compare one block only, at one size. A real U-Net has attention at several resolutions, and we didn't add them up.
No render compares the two, because a model can't be switched between them.
